items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4962

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the agriculture and markets law, in
relation to the humane destruction or disposition of certain animals;
and repealing certain provisions of such law relating thereto

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL : To ensure that when it is necessary
to euthanize an animal, it is done in the most humane manner possible

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS : Section one repeals subdivisions
2-a, 2-b, 2c, 2-d and 2-e of section 374 of the agriculture and
markets law. Section two amends subdivisions 1 and 2 of section 374 of
the agriculture and markets law, as added by chapter 545 of the laws
of 1971, by replacing "the American Society for the Prevention of
Cruelty to Animals" with "a duly incorporated society for the
prevention of cruelty to animals, animal shelter, humane society" as
those who may lawfully cause to be humanely destroyed certain
specified animals.  Subdivision one provides that a licensed
veterinarian shall certify in writing when an animal is maimed,
diseased, disabled or infirmed so as to be unfit for any useful
purpose or, in his or her opinion, humane euthanasia is warranted; or
two reputable citizens called by any agent or officer of a duly
incorporated society for the prevention of cruelty to animals, animal
shelter or humane society or called by a police officer may make the
same finding. This subdivision of the bill also adds that an animal
may be lawfully and humanely destroyed if such animal's suffering
cannot otherwise be alleviated. Subdivision two provides that in the
absence of such findings or certificate, a duly incorporated society
for the prevention of cruelty to animals, animal shelter, or humane
society may make available for adoption or humanely destroy an animal
after five days.

Section three renumbers subdivisions 3, 4, and 5 of section 374 of the
agriculture and markets law 6, 7, and 8, respectively. New
subdivisions 3, 4, and 5 are added. Paragraph a of new subdivision 3
provides that, unless in cases of emergency where euthanasia of an
animal by gunshot is permitted pursuant to subdivision 4 of this
section, euthanasia of an animal shall be accomplished solely by means
of injection of sodium pentobarbital or sodium pentobarbital solution
administered by a certified euthanasia technician, a licensed
veterinarian or a licensed veterinary technician on an animal that is
heavily sedated, anesthetized or comatose. Paragraph b of subdivision
3 provides that no animal shall be left unattended between the time
the euthanasia procedure begins and death is confirmed. The body of a
euthanized animal shall not be disposed of in any manner until death
is confirmed by specified persons.  A violation of paragraph b shall
be punishable by a civil penalty of not more than five hundred
dollars. The department shall promulgate regulations necessary for
implementation of the provisions of this subdivision including those
governing the training and certification of certified euthanasia
technicians. Paragraph a of new subdivision 4 provides that any other
method of euthanasia is prohibited except euthanasia by gunshot is
permissible as an emergency measure when an animal is posing an
imminent threat of serious physical injury to a person or to another
animal or where the use of a humane method of euthanasia is rendered
impossible or in cases where a severely injured animal is suffering
and cannot otherwise be aided. Paragraph b of new subdivision 4
provides that any chamber used to induce hypoxia by means of a lethal
gas shall be dismantled, rendered inoperable and beyond repair, and
removed from the premises within ninety days of the effective date of
this legislation. Violation of paragraph b of new subdivision 4 shall
be punishable by a civil penalty of not more than five hundred
dollars. New subdivision 5 provides that no dog or cat shall be
released from the custody or control of any pound, shelter or other
places listed in this subdivision, unless for the purpose of adoption
or redemption by its owner, and a violation of such subdivision or
subdivision two, three or four of section 374 shall constitute a
misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment for not more than one year, or
by a fine of not more than one thousand dollars, or both.

Section four amends paragraphs band e of subdivision 8 of section 374
of the agriculture and markets law, as added by chapter 569 of the
laws of 1995, by renumbering subdivisions two-a, two-b, two-c and
two-d subdivisions two, three, four and five respectively.

Section five amends section 332 of the agriculture and markets law, as
amended by chapter 674 of the laws of 1980 by providing that when an
animal is euthanized it shall be in accordance with the provisions of
section three hundred seventy-four of this chapter.

Section six amends subdivisions seven and seven-a of section 118 of
the agriculture and markets law by providing that subdivisions two-a,
two-b, two-c, two-d and two-e shall no longer be applicable because
this legislation repeals such subdivisions.

Section seven provides the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :  This legislation simply updates the outmoded New
York State law governing euthanasia of animals taken in by shelters,
humane societies and SPCAs to ensure that when it is necessary,
euthanasia is performed in the most humane manner possible. To this
end, the-bill requires that, except in limited circumstances,
euthanasia be performed by injection of sodium pentobarbital or sodium
pentobarbital solution by a licensed veterinarian, euthanasia
technician or veterinary technician on an animal that is heavily
sedated, anesthetized or comatose.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY : A.5399-C 2008, passed assembly. A.5399-A,
2008, passed assembly. A.5399-A 2007, passed assembly. A.12055, 2006
referred to agriculture committee.

 FISCAL IMPLICATION : None to the state.

 EFFECTIVE DATE : This act shall take effect on the three hundred
sixty-fifth day after it shall become a law.

Section four amends paragraphs band e of subdivision 8 of section 374

This legislation simply updates the outmoded New York State law

end, the bill requires that, except in clearly outlined and limited
circumstances, euthanasia shall be performed by injection of sodium
pentobarbital or sodium pentobarbital solution by a licensed
veterinarian, euthanasia technician or veterinary technician on an
animal that is heavily sedated, anesthetized or comatose.

Additionally, this legislation clearly outlines when euthanasia by
intracardiac injection of sodium pentobarbital or sodium pentobarbital
solution, performed only by a licensed veterinarian, shall be
permitted.

A.5399-C 2008, passed assembly.  A.5399-A,2008, passed assembly.
